question.:question/problem:
Find where the normal line to the curve $y=-4\sqrt{x}-2x$ at the point with $x$-coordinate $4$ intersects the $y$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First find the point on the curve.

$$
f(4)=-4\sqrt{(4)}-2(4)=-16.
$$

The normal passes through $(4,-16)$.

Rewrite the radical or reciprocal using powers, then differentiate.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=- 4 x^{\frac{1}{2}} - 2 x, \\f'(x)&=-2 - \frac{2}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=-2 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(4)&=-2 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{(4)}}=-3, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(-3)}=\frac{1}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(4,-16)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(-16)&=\frac{1}{3}(x-(4)), \\y&=\frac{x}{3} - \frac{52}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=\frac{1}{3}\cdot 0+\left(- \frac{52}{3}\right), \\y&=- \frac{52}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $\left(0,- \frac{52}{3}\right)$.

Rewrite the radical or reciprocal using powers, then differentiate.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=- 4 x^{\frac{1}{2}} - 2 x - 1, \\f'(x)&=-2 - \frac{2}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=-2 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(1)&=-2 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{(1)}}=-4, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(-4)}=\frac{1}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(1,-7)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(-7)&=\frac{1}{4}(x-(1)), \\y&=\frac{x}{4} - \frac{29}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=\frac{1}{4}x+\left(- \frac{29}{4}\right), \\x&=29.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(29,0)$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
First find the point on the curve.

$$
f(4)=-4\sqrt{(4)}-2(4)-2=-18.
$$

The normal passes through $(4,-18)$.

Rewrite the radical or reciprocal using powers, then differentiate.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=- 4 x^{\frac{1}{2}} - 2 x - 2, \\f'(x)&=-2 - \frac{2}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=-2 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(4)&=-2 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{(4)}}=-3, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(-3)}=\frac{1}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(4,-18)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(-18)&=\frac{1}{3}(x-(4)), \\y&=\frac{x}{3} - \frac{58}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find where the normal line to the curve $y=-2\sqrt{x}-2x$ at the point with $x$-coordinate $4$ intersects the $x$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First find the point on the curve.

$$
f(4)=-2\sqrt{(4)}-2(4)=-12.
$$

The normal passes through $(4,-12)$.

Rewrite the radical or reciprocal using powers, then differentiate.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=- 2 x^{\frac{1}{2}} - 2 x, \\f'(x)&=-2 - \frac{1}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=-2 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(4)&=-2 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{(4)}}=- \frac{5}{2}, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{\left(- \frac{5}{2}\right)}=\frac{2}{5}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(4,-12)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(-12)&=\frac{2}{5}(x-(4)), \\y&=\frac{2 x}{5} - \frac{68}{5}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=\frac{2}{5}x+\left(- \frac{68}{5}\right), \\x&=34.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(34,0)$.
